questions.stem: In the intercostal neurovascular bundle just below the rib, which structure is lowest?
How many intercostal muscle layers lie lateral to the costal angle?
Why is the intercostal block placed lateral to the costal angle rather than medial to it?
questions.answer: Medially there is no internal intercostal muscle, only a membrane

questions.stem: At which line does the intercostal lateral cutaneous branch arise, so the block must be proximal to it?
Where is the costal groove deepest, making it in theory the safest site for an intercostal block?
options: Just medial to the rib angle
Just lateral to the rib angle

questions.stem: On which side does an intercostal nerve block produce sensory and motor block at the levels injected?
Which tissues does an intercostal nerve block cover?
Which kinds of procedure suit an intercostal nerve block?
How long does bupivacaine or lidocaine with adrenaline last in an intercostal block?
What is the approximate pneumothorax rate with an intercostal nerve block?
Why is adrenaline added to local anaesthetic for an intercostal block?
questions.answer: Absorption from this site is high; adrenaline reduces systemic uptake

questions.stem: What patient position is used for an intercostal nerve block?
For an intercostal block, how do you find the correct intercostal space?
questions.answer: Count to the right intercostal spaces

questions.stem: For an intercostal block, the rib angle is usually about ____ cm from the midline.
In the landmark intercostal technique, how is the skin handled before the needle goes in?
questions.answer: Pull the skin from the groove up over the rib

questions.stem: In the landmark intercostal technique, at what cephalad angle is the 22G 50-mm needle held?
In the landmark intercostal technique, within about how far should the needle contact the rib?
In the landmark intercostal technique, how is the needle moved after it contacts the rib?
questions.answer: Walk it off the lower edge of the rib, keeping the 20° cephalad angle

questions.stem: In the landmark intercostal technique, how far deeper than the rib does the nerve usually lie?
In the landmark intercostal technique, how much local anaesthetic is injected per level?
When is ultrasound especially helpful for an intercostal block?
questions.answer: Finding the spaces in obesity or difficult anatomy

questions.stem: How is the high-frequency linear probe oriented on the back for an intercostal block?
questions.answer: Vertically (sagittal), to see rib, space and pleura

questions.stem: For an ultrasound-guided intercostal block, where should the scan sit relative to the costal angle and posterior axillary line?
questions.answer: Lateral to the costal angle, but posterior to the posterior axillary line

questions.stem: For an ultrasound-guided intercostal block, which needle direction is used?
With ultrasound guidance, how much local anaesthetic is usually enough per intercostal space?
